ep11: All eight sections and first body section preserved: the 1869–1881 arc from constitutional inclusion to practical repression, without erasing the still-available constitutional promise.
Grant's 1868 election, Black voters, limited political experience, personal honesty distinguished from administration corruption, and federal protection of rights.

Fifteenth Amendment, Reconstruction governments, approximately 2,000 Black officeholders, Revels and Rainey, congressional participation, South Carolina schooling, women's exclusion and discriminatory voting barriers.
Foner and Du Bois, corruption without the racialized double standard, carpetbaggers and scalawags, and comparison with Northern Gilded Age corruption.
Organized Klan terror, Memphis, New Orleans and Colfax, Enforcement Acts, nine South Carolina counties, arrests and the more open 1872 election.
Cruikshank, Slaughter-House, the 1873 panic, Northern racism and declining will, land dependence, and the multicausal collapse of Reconstruction.
Disputed 1876 returns and governments, 185–184 commission outcome, informal compromise and the limited scope of 1877 troop removal; realism-versus-betrayal interpretations.
Conclusion retains real inclusion and real rollback, acknowledgment versus repayment of the constitutional debt, and nonfatalistic contingency.
ep12: All eight sections and first body section preserved: Jim Crow's political, economic and resistance exits closed through institutions, coercion and memory.
Segregation across daily life, Plessy's separate-but-equal reasoning and Harlan's dissent as judicial memory rather than constitutional text.

Mississippi and Louisiana registration figures, nominally neutral voting barriers distinct from explicitly racial white primaries, Williams and Giles, and practical constitutional-enforcement failure.
Black Codes, vagrancy, fines, the Thirteenth Amendment punishment exception, convict leasing, debt peonage, sharecropping and nominal freedom without an effective exit.

Tuskegee's 4,743 people and 1892 figures, EJI third-edition 4,084 victims and 800-person increment, Wells and the three grocery operators, and the author's argument about terror and continued resistance.
Lost Cause organizations, membership, school narratives and monuments; their role in maintaining legitimacy without reducing the entire system to memory politics.
National retreat rather than a South-only account; Black families, churches, schools and organizing; Washington and Du Bois as differing strategies rather than a simplistic right-versus-wrong pair.

Conclusion retains the three exits, the constitutional amendments and dissenting judicial memory, duration distinguished from permanent closure, and the possibility of dismantling a constructed order.
ep13: All nine sections and first body section preserved: 1881–1897 fragmentation, new private economic power, and the distinction between class and belonging.
Garfield's assassination, Arthur's Stalwart background, the Pendleton Act, examinations and employment protections, the commission and initial civil-service coverage.
Railway monopoly and rebates, Standard Oil's trust and refining share, Morgan's gold consortium, and private power outside the original political checks.
Knights of Labor, Black and female membership, child labor, immigration figures, agricultural debt and deflation, Grange, Farmers' Alliances and the People's Party.
Haymarket, Homestead and Pullman with their figures and competing pressures; mail trains, injunctions, federal force, Debs and the argument that order favored capital.
ICC chronology and limited powers, the qualified long-and-short-haul rule, Sherman Act, E. C. Knight and the manufacturing-commerce distinction; the tool also used against labor.
Chinese Exclusion chronology, prior lawful residents and reentry documentation, naturalization exclusion, later extensions and the racial belonging axis.
Cleveland's second term, silver-purchase repeal, gold reserves, Morgan, competing unemployment estimates, Texas relief veto and the first nonconsecutive presidency.
Conclusion retains the mismatch between new private power and weak scattered regulatory capacity, labor repression, exclusion, and early administrative development.
ep14: All eight sections and first body section preserved: the domestic and overseas inclusion problems are connected without being made identical.
Omaha platform, sixteen parts silver to one gold, Bryan's Cross of Gold, McKinley and Hanna's campaign, electoral figures, Populist defeat and the later partial absorption of its agenda.
Cuban independence, reconcentration, newspapers without a single-cause war explanation, the Maine and uncertain explosion evidence, humanitarian justification and imperial consequences.
Manila, Paris treaty terms, Hawaii, executive initiative alongside congressional and Senate roles, Teller's temporary pacification exception and the later Platt framework.

Filipino independence, Aguinaldo, conventional and guerrilla war, continuing resistance, coercive practices, American/Filipino/civilian figures, and Gates's 1981 upper-end 1898–1903 estimate including 1902 cholera.
Anti-Imperialist League, Carnegie, Twain, James and Gompers, the platform, and founding consent principles as an internal standard of criticism.
Insular Cases and the divided Downes opinions, territorial incorporation and partial constitutional application, interpreted as postponement rather than resolution.
Conclusion retains partial domestic incorporation and overseas exclusion, anti-imperial criticism, nonfatalism and the coexistence of universal promises with their violation.
ep15: All nine sections and first body section preserved: McKinley's death and Roosevelt's succession, preexisting institutions and pressures, and EP13's economic-governance-body argument.
Stewardship theory, Jackson and Lincoln versus Buchanan and Taft, constitutional/statutory and reasonably implied powers, and the public-interest rationale with its expansion risks.
Square Deal, Northern Securities, good/bad trusts, 44 suits, strengthened federal oversight, the Bureau of Corporations and Hepburn Act.
Anthracite strike, 147,000 workers, winter emergency, third-party public interest, the EP13 Pullman contrast, Morgan's arbitration and wage/hour outcomes without union recognition.
The Jungle, prior food bills, Neill–Reynolds investigation, 1906 food and meat laws, conservation acreage and institutional examples.
Big Stick, Panama, Colombia, the canal zone and congressional context, Roosevelt Corollary and international police power, with fewer external checks abroad.
Booker T. Washington's dinner, racist response, Brownsville alibis, 167 soldiers in three companies and discharge without honor; progress on one axis and racial retreat on another.
Taft succession, later split, New Nationalism and legalism; liberal, revisionist and social-control interpretations without a heroic or publicity-only reduction.
Conclusion retains stronger administrative capacity coupled to executive expansion, future precedent and unequal inclusion; backward references identify EP13 or earlier essays.

editorial_policy: Preserve every substantive argument, example and qualification in the full Chinese baseline. Use local native/fidelity edits and root-authorized factual calibration only; no compressed rewrite, thesis substitution, or paragraph deletion.
factual_verification_scope: Historical primary-source verification was performed/coordinated by root. This review independently read all Chinese and DE/FR essays, raised concrete questions, then applied only the shared approved factual scope; it does not claim independent primary-source re-verification of every historical statement.
root_authorized_calibrations: EP11: Attribute the strong Grant honesty assessment to the Miller Center account, not all modern historians.
EP11: Refer to Republican governments in multiple Southern states during Reconstruction, not every state in 1870.
EP11–12: The Fifteenth Amendment's practical enforcement failed to stop discriminatory barriers; it did not legally authorize racial discrimination.
EP11–12: The 1877 withdrawal removed protection from remaining Reconstruction governments and returned those troops to barracks, not all forces out of the South.
EP12: The Civil Rights Cases invalidated public-accommodation equality provisions and associated remedies, not the entire 1875 statute.
EP12: The Memphis grocery lynching involved three Black operators.
EP12: Retain EJI third-edition 4,084 and at least 800 additional people, explicitly counted as victims rather than separate incidents; do not mix with the current webpage's other edition.
EP13: Existing regulatory foundations were weak and scattered, not nonexistent.
EP13: Qualify the long-and-short-haul rule by comparable conditions, same line/direction and inclusion of the shorter journey in the longer.
EP13: Sherman-law tools were also deployed against labor, not before all capital cases.
EP14: The ratio is sixteen weight parts silver to one gold; French was already explicit.
EP14: Executive initiative retained congressional authorization and declaration-of-war requirements, and Senate treaty consent.
EP14: Gates's 1981 upper-end estimate covers 1898–1903 related total mortality including his 1902 cholera count.
EP15: Taft's powers derive from Constitution or statute and reasonably implied authority, not only explicit constitutional grants.
EP15: Roosevelt more forcefully established federal economic oversight, not for the first time.
EP15: The opening economic-governance-body quotation belongs to EP13; the conclusion refers to earlier essays rather than EP14 alone.
EP15: The coal-strike episode strengthens an important institutional channel; it is not the first labor arbitration or previously nonexistent nonviolent route.
EP15: The conclusion describes expansion and integration of existing regulatory foundations, consistent with the opening's acknowledgment of the 1887 ICC.

changes.before: Nach ausdrücklichem Urteil der neueren Forschung war Grant selbst nie Ziel der Ermittlungen. Seine persönliche Redlichkeit stand nicht infrage, und aus den Skandalen zog er keinen eigenen Gewinn.
changes.after: Eine historische Darstellung des Miller Center hält ausdrücklich fest, Grant selbst sei nie Ziel der Ermittlungen gewesen, seine persönliche Redlichkeit habe nicht infrage gestanden, und aus den Skandalen habe er keinen eigenen Gewinn gezogen.
changes.rationale: Attribute the strong claim to the verified Miller Center account, not a consensus of all modern scholarship.

changes.before: Bis 1870 hatten die Republikaner die Regierungen der Südstaaten unter ihre Kontrolle gebracht, und schwarze Abgeordnete zogen in die Parlamente der Bundesstaaten ein.
changes.after: Während der Reconstruction kontrollierten die Republikaner zeitweilig die Regierungen mehrerer Südstaaten, und schwarze Abgeordnete zogen in die Parlamente der Bundesstaaten ein.
changes.rationale: Do not imply Republican control of every Southern state in 1870.

changes.before: Deshalb konnten die Südstaaten seinen Wortlaut später mit scheinbar neutralen Regelungen wie Lese- und Schreibtests, Großvaterklauseln und Wahlsteuern umgehen.
changes.after: In der Praxis konnten die Südstaaten seine Garantien später mit scheinbar neutralen, aber diskriminierend angewandten Regelungen wie Lese- und Schreibtests, Großvaterklauseln und Wahlsteuern unterlaufen.
changes.rationale: Distinguish practical evasion and discriminatory enforcement from constitutionally lawful permission.

changes.before: Er verbot aber keine Hürden, die Rasse nicht beim Namen nannten und dennoch eigens gegen Schwarze gerichtet waren; ein solches Verbot war auch schwer zu fassen.
changes.after: Seine Garantien verhinderten in der Praxis jedoch nicht, dass Hürden errichtet und diskriminierend angewandt wurden, die Rasse nicht beim Namen nannten und dennoch eigens gegen Schwarze gerichtet waren.
changes.rationale: The Fifteenth Amendment did not legally authorize deliberately racial barriers; the failure was practical enforcement.

changes.before: zur sogenannten örtlichen Selbstregierung überging, Truppen abzog, den weißen Demokraten des Südens entgegenkam
changes.after: zur sogenannten örtlichen Selbstregierung überging, die zum Schutz der letzten Reconstruction-Regierungen an den Regierungssitzen eingesetzten Truppen in die Kasernen zurückführte, den weißen Demokraten des Südens entgegenkam
changes.rationale: Specify removal of protective troops from the remaining state-government seats to barracks, not evacuation of all troops from the South.

changes.before: Les recherches récentes sont explicites : Grant lui-même n’a jamais été visé par les enquêtes, son honnêteté personnelle n’a pas été mise en cause et il n’a tiré aucun profit privé de ces affaires.
changes.after: Une présentation historique du Miller Center l’affirme explicitement : Grant lui-même n’a jamais été visé par les enquêtes, son honnêteté personnelle n’a pas été mise en cause et il n’a tiré aucun profit privé de ces affaires.

changes.before: En 1870, les républicains contrôlent les gouvernements des États sudistes et des élus noirs siègent dans leurs assemblées législatives.
changes.after: Pendant la Reconstruction, les républicains contrôlent, pour un temps, les gouvernements de plusieurs États du Sud et des élus noirs siègent dans leurs assemblées législatives.
changes.rationale: Do not imply Republican control of every Southern state in 1870.

changes.before: C’est pourquoi les États du Sud pourront plus tard contourner sa lettre par des dispositifs apparemment neutres : tests d’alphabétisation, clauses dites « du grand-père » et taxes électorales.
changes.after: Dans les faits, les États du Sud parviendront plus tard à vider ses garanties de leur effet par des dispositifs apparemment neutres mais appliqués de façon discriminatoire : tests d’alphabétisation, clauses dites « du grand-père » et taxes électorales.
changes.rationale: Distinguish practical evasion and discriminatory enforcement from constitutionally lawful permission.

changes.before: Il n’interdisait pas, et pouvait difficilement interdire, des conditions qui ne nomment jamais la race tout en visant expressément les Noirs.
changes.after: Ses garanties n’ont pourtant pas empêché, dans la pratique, la mise en place et l’application discriminatoire de conditions qui ne nomment jamais la race tout en visant expressément les Noirs.
changes.rationale: The Fifteenth Amendment did not legally authorize deliberately racial barriers; the failure was practical enforcement.

changes.before: se rallie à la prétendue autonomie locale, retire les troupes, apaise les démocrates blancs du Sud
changes.after: se rallie à la prétendue autonomie locale, ramène dans leurs casernes les troupes qui protégeaient les sièges des derniers gouvernements de la Reconstruction, apaise les démocrates blancs du Sud
changes.rationale: Specify removal of protective troops from the remaining state-government seats to barracks, not evacuation of all troops from the South.

changes.before: Vom Abzug der Bundestruppen 1877 bis in die ersten Jahre des 20. Jahrhunderts
changes.after: Vom Ende des militärischen Schutzes der letzten Reconstruction-Regierungen 1877 bis in die ersten Jahre des 20. Jahrhunderts

changes.before: Die Civil Rights Cases von 1883 brachten das Bürgerrechtsgesetz von 1875 zu Fall.
changes.after: Die Civil Rights Cases von 1883 brachten die Bestimmungen des Bürgerrechtsgesetzes von 1875 über den gleichberechtigten Zugang zu öffentlich zugänglichen Einrichtungen und die zugehörigen Rechtsmittel zu Fall.
changes.rationale: Limit the invalidation to the public-accommodation equality provisions and remedies, not the entire statute.

changes.before: Politisch bestand der zentrale Mechanismus der Schließung darin, die vom 15. Verfassungszusatz zugelassene formale Neutralität zu einem Werkzeug rassisch selektiver Rechtsanwendung zu machen.
changes.after: Politisch bestand der zentrale Mechanismus der Schließung darin, formal rassenneutral formulierte Zugangshürden zu einem Werkzeug rassisch selektiver Rechtsanwendung zu machen, gegen die sich die Garantien des 15. Verfassungszusatzes in der Praxis nicht durchsetzten.
changes.rationale: Do not describe discriminatory implementation as authorized by the amendment.

changes.before: Nachdem 1892 in Memphis ein schwarzer Inhaber eines von Schwarzen geführten Lebensmittelgeschäfts gelyncht worden war,
changes.after: Nachdem 1892 in Memphis drei schwarze Betreiber eines Lebensmittelgeschäfts gelyncht worden waren,
changes.rationale: The Memphis grocery-store lynching involved three Black men, not a single proprietor.

changes.before: Eine neuere Untersuchung rassistischer Terrorlynchmorde ermittelte für zwölf Südstaaten zwischen 1877 und 1950 insgesamt 4.084 Fälle. Das waren mindestens 800 mehr als in der zuvor umfassendsten älteren Erhebung.
changes.after: Die dritte Ausgabe des Berichts der Equal Justice Initiative erfasste für zwölf Südstaaten zwischen 1877 und 1950 insgesamt 4.084 schwarze Opfer rassistischer Terrorlynchmorde. Das waren mindestens 800 Menschen mehr als in der zuvor umfassendsten älteren Erhebung.
changes.rationale: Identify the EJI third-edition count and use victims, not separate incidents, for both 4,084 and 800.

changes.before: und die zugehörigen Rechtsmittel zu Fall.
changes.after: und die zugehörigen Rechtsschutzbestimmungen zu Fall.
changes.rationale: Use the precise German term for the remedial provisions invalidated with the public-accommodations rules; Rechtsmittel would misleadingly suggest appellate remedies.

changes.after: McKinley pouvait donner à ces démarches une impulsion particulièrement forte. Elles exigeaient néanmoins les autorisations législatives et la déclaration de guerre du Congrès, ainsi que le consentement du Sénat au traité.
changes.rationale: Preserve executive initiative without erasing congressional authorization, the declaration of war, or Senate treaty consent.

changes.before: En 1981, John M. Gates estimait que l’ensemble des décès liés à la guerre entre 1898 et 1903 pouvait atteindre environ 321 000.
changes.after: En 1981, John M. Gates estimait que l’ensemble des décès liés à la guerre entre 1898 et 1903 pouvait atteindre environ 321 000, en incluant les morts du choléra de 1902 qu’il retenait dans son calcul.
changes.rationale: Define Gates's upper-end estimate as 1898–1903 war-related total deaths including his 1902 cholera count, not a recent civilian consensus.

changes.before: Pour les seconds, seule une compétence explicitement conférée par la Constitution autorise le président à agir.
changes.after: Pour Taft, l’action du président doit se fonder sur les pouvoirs conférés par la Constitution ou par la loi, y compris ceux que l’on peut raisonnablement en déduire ; le seul besoin national ne crée pas de pouvoir supplémentaire.
changes.rationale: Represent Taft's constitutional/statutory and reasonably implied powers accurately; not constitutional express powers alone.

changes.before: En affirmant le principe du contrôle, elle annonce pour la première fois que l’échiquier économique relève, lui aussi, de sa compétence.
changes.after: En affirmant le principe du contrôle, elle établit plus clairement et plus fermement que l’échiquier économique relève, lui aussi, de sa compétence.
changes.rationale: Roosevelt strengthened and clarified an existing regulatory principle rather than first inventing economic oversight.

changes.before: Pour les premiers, il peut agir pourvu que cela soit véritablement nécessaire à la nation et ne lui soit pas expressément interdit.
changes.after: Pour Roosevelt, le président peut agir pourvu que cela soit véritablement nécessaire à la nation et ne lui soit pas expressément interdit.
changes.rationale: Restore an explicit antecedent after the preceding sentence names Taft, preserving the stewardship-theory contrast without a dangling group reference.
